review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. NOAA archival tagging of 173 adults and 41 recaptures supports seasonal ambient-temperature and depth use; vertical depth is not identical to seafloor bathymetry.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for white seabass.
factors.value_notes: Aalbers and Sepulveda deployed 173 depth/temperature tags on adult white seabass and recovered 41 fish, yielding 9,130 days of records. Ambient temperature ranged 8.7-23.6 °C (mean 15.2 °C); 52% of time was 13-16 °C, with a peak around 14 °C, and 95% of surface-oriented records occurred at 12-19 °C. This supports thermal relevance, but ambient temperature at fish depth is not always satellite SST; the configured 14-22 °C range and 16-20 °C ideal are shifted warmer than the central observed temperatures.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for white seabass.
factors.value_notes: The same adult tagging study found 95% of vertical depth records shallower than 50 m, with a maximum of 245 m and seasonal deeper winter profiles. CDFW describes white seabass as a nearshore/inner-shelf species commonly caught in 3-27 m. These support a shallow coastal context, but fish vertical depth is not seafloor bathymetry; the configured 2-40 m band and 4-35 m ideal are not a measured bottom-depth preference curve.
